pilot_inputs.title: PILOT Input Files and Sampling Configuration
pilot_inputs.content:
<data_description>PILOT generates 3D candidate ligands conditioned on a protein binding pocket using its included CrossDocked checkpoint. Inference uses checkpoint-derived priors and the reference ligand atom count, and does not require the training dataset. The protein PDB and reference-ligand SDF must use the same coordinate frame.</data_description>

<input_files>
[.pdb, .sdf, .json]
</input_files>

<input_schema>
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "num_samples": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 100, "default": 10},
    "batch_size": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 40, "default": 10},
    "max_sample_iter": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 50, "default": 20},
    "pocket_cutoff": {"type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0, "maximum": 12, "default": 7.0},
    "filter_by_lipinski": {"type": "boolean", "default": false}
  }
}
</input_schema>

Provide exactly one protein PDB and one reference-ligand SDF whose coordinates share a frame, and at most one optional JSON configuration. If no pocket residue list is supplied, the service selects standard protein residues within `pocket_cutoff` angstroms of the reference ligand. Output structures are candidate molecules; the summary does not report affinity, docking scores, or experimental results.

pilot_paper.title: PILOT Research Paper
pilot_paper.content: <data_description>PILOT is an equivariant diffusion approach for pocket-conditioned de novo ligand generation with multi-objective guidance via importance sampling. This serving configuration exposes ligand sampling using the included CrossDocked checkpoint and does not calculate binding affinity or docking scores.</data_description>
